full_text_zh:
[P1] 猴王出世
《西游记》之一
原著 吴承恩
改编 卢光照
绘画 张树德
河北美术出版社

[P2] 内容提要
西游记的故事，多少年来在群众中广为流传，深受欢迎。为此，我们根据古典神话名著《西游记》编绘了这套连环画，共三十五册，以飨读者。
这是第一册，主要描绘古时候有座花果山，山上有块仙石，日久天长，变成了一个仙猴。他占据水帘洞为王，众猴称他为“猴王”。这猴王聪明机智，天不怕，地不怕。为了学到通天本领，他不避艰险，远涉重洋，在灵台方寸山，访到了须菩提祖师，练会了驾筋斗云、七十二般变化的神通。然后又回到花果山水帘洞，驱逐了侵占洞府的妖魔，率领群猴，苦练本领，过起无拘无束的猴王生活。
1 相传在古代东胜神州，有个傲来国。国近大海，海内有一座名山，叫做花果山。

[P3] 2 山顶上有块仙石。仙石受了天真地秀，日精月华，便
有通灵之意。内育仙胞，日久天长，化作一个石猴。
3 那猴在山中，行走跳跃，吃草木，喝山泉，和狼虫
虎豹为伴。到了夜间，就睡在山崖下。无拘无束，好不自在。

[P4] 4 一日，天气炎热，那猴和群猴到山涧洗澡，众猴都说：‘这股水不知是哪里来的，我们今天闲暇无事，顺涧边找源头玩耍去吧！’一声喊叫，群猴都向源头跑去。
5 到了源流之处，原来是一股瀑布飞泉。众猴都拍手称赞道：‘好水！好水！’又道：‘哪一个敢钻进去找到源头出来，不伤身体，我们就拜他为王。’

[P5] 6 忽然猴群中跳出一个石猴，应声高叫道：‘我进去！我进去！’只见他两眼一闭，将身一纵，跳到瀑布中去了。
7 到了水中，那里却无水无波，只见明明朗朗的一座桥。他到了桥上，向前一看，好似有人家居住。

[P6] 8 石猴过了桥，到跟前一看，却是一个石洞，洞内有石灶、石碗、石盆、石床、石凳。中间一块石碑上，刻着“花果山福地，水帘洞洞天”。
9 石猴喜欢异常，急急抽身往外走，跳出水外。众猴都围上来问道：“里面怎么样？水有多深？”石猴笑道：“好造化！好造化！里面不但没水，而且是个好住处哩！”把详情说了一遍。

[P7] 10 群猴都愿搬进去住，就说：‘你还是先走，带我们进去！’石猴纵身往里一跳，说道：‘都随我进来！’那些大大小小的猴，一个个跟了进去。
11 到了石洞，众猴个个抢盆夺碗，占灶争床，搬过来，移过去，直到疲倦了才止。

[P8] 12 石猴这时端坐在上面道：‘你们都说谁有本领进来，就拜他为王，我如今进进出出，给你们找了这所好住处，该拜我为王了吧。’众猴听了，立刻朝上礼拜，口称‘千岁大王’。
13 石猴从此便叫做‘美猴王’了。他分派了君臣佐使。朝游花果山，暮宿水帘洞，好不快活。一日，与群猴饮宴，忽然落下泪来。

[P9] 14 众猴慌忙拜倒问其根由。原来猴王觉得现在虽然不归人王法律，不怕禽兽侵袭，一旦老死，还要受阎王管束。众猴得知此情，个个悲伤。
15 忽然，一个通背猿猴跳出来叫道：‘大王不必悲啼，我听说佛、仙、神、圣均能躲过轮回，不生不灭，与天地齐寿，何不访求个不老之术？’猴王一听大喜。决定明天下山四处访问。

[P10] 16 次日一早，猴王吃过饯行宴，叫众猴给他用枯枝编成筏子，取根竹竿作篙，装载些果品吃食，独自登筏，用篙一撑，飘飘荡荡，向大海去了。
17 连日刮起东南风，不几日把他送到西北岸上。这里是南赡部洲地界。他上得岸来，只见海边有人捕鱼、打雁、淘盐……。他走到跟前，做个鬼脸，吓得那些人都四散逃走。

[P11] 18 其中有个跑得慢的，被他捉住。猴王剥了他的衣裳，穿在自己身上，便摇摇摆摆，学作人的样子，穿州过府，四处去访问仙道。
19 转眼就是八九年，一日访游到西牛贺洲地界。听得树林深处有歌唱之声：“……相逢处，非仙即道，静坐诵黄庭。”他想：“黄庭”是道德真言，这人必定是神仙。

[P12] 20 他走过去一看，原来是一个樵夫在那里砍柴。猴王把来意一说，樵夫道：‘我并非神仙，不过我和神仙相邻，此歌为他们所教，若有烦恼苦情，唱唱自然解愁。’
21 猴王一听大喜，就叫樵夫指给神仙的住处。樵夫向前一指说：‘前面山中有座斜月三星洞，洞里有个神仙叫须菩提祖师。他教出的徒弟不计其数，现在还有三四十人跟他修行。’

[P13] 22 猴王顺着樵夫指的方向走去，约七八里远，果然有一座洞府。洞门紧闭，静悄悄无有一人。抬头一看，见崖头石额碑上有十个大字：‘灵台方寸山，斜月三星洞’。
23 猴王看了半天，不敢敲门。这时肚子有些饥饿，便跳上松树，摘些松子来吃。正吃间，只听‘呀’的一声，洞门开处，走出一个仙童。

[P14] 24 那仙童高叫道：‘什么人在此骚扰？’猴王赶忙跳了下来道：‘我是个访仙学道的弟子。不敢在此骚扰。’仙童道：‘我家师父说外边有修行人来了，叫我出来接待，原来是你，快跟我来。’
25 猴王到了洞里，只见菩提祖师正端坐在台上讲道，两边有三十个小仙侍立台下。猴王一见，倒身下拜，磕头不计其数，口中只道：‘师父！师父！弟子我志心朝礼，志心朝礼。’

[P15] 26 祖师问道：‘你从哪里来？姓什名谁？’猴王道：‘我从东胜神洲来。是石头里生的，没有姓名。’祖师道：‘既然你远道来投，我就收你为徒！’并给他起名叫‘孙悟空’。
27 美猴王自有了姓名，更是喜欢非常。每日和众师兄学言语礼貌，讲经论道；闲时扫地锄园，养花修树，不觉在洞中过了六七年。

[P16] 28 一日，祖师登台讲道，众仙无不洗耳静听。孙悟空越听越得意，抓耳挠腮，眉开眼笑，忍不住舞蹈起来。
29 祖师正讲得入神，忽见悟空这般状态，就喝问道：
“你不用心听讲，为何颠狂跃舞？”悟空忙道：“弟子实是诚心听讲，只因听到妙处，喜不自胜。望师父恕罪！”

[P17] 30 祖师道：‘既然如此，我问你想学什么道？’悟空道：‘任凭师父传授。’祖师便把‘术’、‘流’、‘静’、‘动’几门道都说与他听。悟空觉得这些道门不能长生不老，不愿意学。
31 祖师‘咚’的一声，跳下讲台，手持戒尺，指定悟空道：‘你这样不学，那样不学，要学什么？’走上前，将悟空头上打了三下，倒背着手，走入里面，将中门关了，撇下大众而去。

[P18] 32 众师兄见师父这般情况，都埋怨悟空。悟空一点儿不恼，因为他已打破盘中之谜，知道打他三下是叫三更时分存心；倒背着手，将中门关上，是叫他从后门进去在秘处传道给他。
33 当日夜间，悟空等众师兄都入睡后，便轻轻起来穿上衣服，偷开前门，走了出来。

[P19] 34 悟空走到后门，只见门儿虚掩，便推门进去，到了祖师床前，见祖师已朝里睡着。悟空不敢惊动，便跪在床前等候。
35 不多时祖师醒来。悟空忙上前道：‘师父，弟子在此等多时了。’祖师喝道：‘你不在前边睡觉，却来后边作甚？’悟空道：‘师父昨天坛前允我三更从后门进来到此传道，故大胆前来。’

[P20] 36 祖师一听大喜，暗想：这猢狲果然是天地生成的！不然，怎能打破我盘中之谜？接着对悟空道：“也是你我有缘，就把长生妙道传给你吧！”说罢便将长生口诀教给了悟空。
37 悟空学会长生妙诀，叩谢了师父，从后门又悄悄溜回前边。这时天已发亮，他坐在原来睡的地方，故意大声喊道：“天亮了！天亮了！起来呀！”众师兄都被他吵醒起来。

[P21] 38 悟空在山中学道，不觉又过了三年。一天，祖师登台，问悟空道：“你学的怎样了？”悟空上前叩头道：“弟子近来法性颇通，根源也渐稳固。”祖师道：“很好，只是要防‘三灾利害’。
39 悟空沉思很久道：“我已炼成长生不老，还怕什么三灾？”祖师道：“这是非常之道。五百年后，天降雷灾打你；再五百年，天降火灾烧你；再五百年，天降风灾吹你！须要设法躲过。”

[P22] 40 悟空一听，吓得连忙叩头道：‘万望师父传我躲避三灾之法，恩情终生不忘！’祖师见悟空心诚，便道：‘也好，你且附耳过来。’便把七十二变的口诀教给他了。
41 悟空自得道后，天天苦学苦练，渐渐精通起来。忽一日，祖师与众徒弟在三星洞前玩赏晚景，问悟空道：‘你练得怎样了？’

[P23] 42 悟空道：‘弟子已学成功，可以霞举飞升了。’祖师道：‘很好。你就飞举一次给我看看。’悟空把身一纵，打了个连扯跟头，跳离地面五六丈，踏云霞而去。
43 约有顿饭时候，来去才不过三里远近，又落在面前。祖师笑道：‘这算不得腾云，只算得爬云。腾云清早起到天晚，可以把四海都游遍了，像你这本领，还差得远哩！’

[P24] 44 悟空连三叩头道：‘万望师父舍个大慈悲，将这腾云之法，一发传给我吧！’祖师道：‘凡诸仙腾云，都是跌脚而起，你却不是这样。就你的姿势，传你个“筋斗云”吧！’
45 祖师附耳把“筋斗云”的口诀教给了悟空后，说道：‘你只要念动真言，攥紧拳头，将身一抖，跳将起来，一筋斗就可翻十万八千里！’大家听了，无不羡慕悟空有造化。

[P25] 46 一天，几个徒弟在松树下会讲，会讲完毕便对悟空道：‘悟空，你运气真好，师父传授给你躲三灾变化之法，现在练得怎样了？变给我们看看如何？’
47 悟空道：‘不瞒兄长，因我昼夜苦练，现已全会。你们出个题目，我给你们变变看。’大家都说：‘变棵松树吧。’悟空念动咒语，摇身一变，果然变成了一棵松树。

[P26] 48 大家见悟空变成松树，都拍手叫好。不料却惊动了师父，出来问道：‘谁在此喧闹？’大家见师父出来了，个个整衣向前，悟空也显了本相，躲在人背后道：‘启禀师父，我们在这里会讲，并无外姓喧闹。’
49 师父大怒道：‘你们哪像修行的样子！’大家见师父火了，便把悟空变松树的事说了一遍。师父随即道：‘既然这样你们先走吧，悟空留在这里我有话讲。’

[P27] 50 师父把悟空叫到跟前道：‘你变什么松树，学了这点功夫就在人前卖弄，这岂不是高傲自满？’悟空连忙叩头认错。
51 师父道：‘我也不怪你，你快回水帘洞去吧，要记住，所学本领只能行侠做义，不准胡作非为。’悟空道：‘师父言语，我岂敢忘，只是师恩未报，心中不安！’师父道：‘只要你心中有我也就算了。去吧！’

[P28] 52 悟空无奈，只得谢过师父，念着咒语，纵起“筋斗云”，回花果山去了。
53 不消一个时辰，早看见花果山水帘洞，他便按下云头，落在花果山上，大声叫道：‘孩儿们，我回来了！’

[P29] 54 这时大小猴子，都从石崖下，花木中，树林里跳了出来，把悟空团团围住，问长问短，好不喜欢。
55 其中有些猴便向悟空诉苦，说有个混世魔王，常来这里欺侮他们，抢他们的东西，掳他们的子侄，还要强占水帘洞！悟空一听怒道：“他在哪里住？我去报仇！”

[P30] 56 众猴把混世魔王的来路方向指给悟空，只见他一个“筋斗云”便不见了。
57 悟空正在云中行走，从云头里看见下边山崖下有几个小妖在跳舞，他想：这里一定就是了。

[P31] 58 悟空降落下来，把个小妖吓得乱跑，悟空道：“别跑！快去报告你们的混世魔王，就说花果山水帘洞洞主找他算帐来了。”
59 小妖们进洞飞报给魔王。魔王道：“快把我的披挂兵器拿来！”魔王穿了甲胄，拿了一把大刀，与众妖出了洞。高叫道：“哪个水帘洞主？敢在这里取闹？”

[P32] 60 悟空道：‘你这恶魔，有眼不识老孙，请吃老孙几拳！’
说着，劈脸打去。魔王举起大刀，朝悟空砍来。
61 悟空见来势凶猛，抵挡不住，便使了个身外身的法术，拔一把毫毛，在嘴中一嚼，喷了出去，叫声‘变！’立刻变了二三百猴子，围住了魔王。

[P33] 62 这群猴子扯的扯，抱的抱，立刻把魔王扳倒。悟空过来，夺了大刀，分开小猴，照魔王顶门一下，砍为两半。接着，他们把洞里的妖魔都杀光了。
63 他又把毫毛一抖，众猴都收到身上，那些没有收到身上的，都是魔王从水帘洞掳来的。众猴把情况一说，悟空道：“既然都是水帘洞儿孙，跟我一块回去吧！”众猴个个欢喜若狂。

[P34] 64 临行，悟空放了一把火，烧了魔洞，然后叫几十个小猴，闭了眼，念了咒语，驾阵狂风，直奔水帘洞去。
65 到了洞口，悟空道：‘孩儿们，睁眼。’众猴儿认得是家乡，个个喜欢，都奔回洞去。

[P35] 66 众猴们父子团圆，猴王又远游归来，自是喜上加喜，便把各色好酒，各色鲜果拿了出来，大家欢欢乐乐，饮起团圆酒来。此后，悟空操练猴兵，保卫花果山。欲知详情，请看第二册《龙宫借宝》。

[P1] The Birth of the Monkey King
Part One of Journey to the West
Original work by Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by Lu Guangzhao
Illustrated by Zhang Shude
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

[P2] Content Summary
The story of Journey to the West has been widely circulated and deeply loved by the public for many years. For this reason, we have compiled this set of illustrated books based on the classical mythological masterpiece "Journey to the West", totaling thirty-five volumes, to delight readers.
This is the first volume, mainly depicting an ancient Flower-Fruit Mountain, where there was a magical stone that, over time, transformed into a divine monkey. He took over the Water Curtain Cave as king, and the monkeys called him "Monkey King". This Monkey King was intelligent and fearless, neither afraid of heaven nor earth. To master supernatural skills, he braved dangers and crossed the vast ocean, reaching Lingtai Fangcun Mountain, where he met Master Subodhi and learned the skills of somersault cloud and seventy-two transformations. He then returned to the Water Curtain Cave on Flower-Fruit Mountain, drove out the demons who had occupied the cave, led the monkeys, practiced his skills, and lived a carefree life as the Monkey King.
1 It is said that in ancient Dongsheng神州, there was a country called Aolai. Near the sea, there was a famous mountain called Flower-Fruit Mountain.

[P3] 2 There is a magical stone on the mountain top. The stone, having absorbed the essence of heaven and earth, the light of the sun and moon, gained the ability to sense the spiritual world. It nurtured a divine embryo, and over time, transformed into a stone monkey.
3 The monkey roamed the mountains, leaping and running, eating plants and drinking mountain springs, accompanied by wolves, insects, tigers, and leopards. At night, it slept beneath the cliff. Free and unrestrained, it was truly carefree.

[P4] 4 One day, the weather was hot, and the monkey and the troop went to bathe in the mountain stream. The monkeys all said, 'We don't know where this water comes from. Since we have nothing to do today, let's follow the stream to find its source and play!' With a shout, the troop rushed toward the source.
5 At the source, they found a cascading waterfall. The monkeys clapped and praised, 'Good water! Good water!' Then they said, 'Whoever dares to go in and find the source, come out unharmed, we will make him our king.'

[P5] 6 Suddenly, a stone monkey jumped out of the monkey crowd and shouted: 'I'll go in! I'll go in!' He closed his eyes, leaped forward, and jumped into the waterfall.
7 When he reached the water, there was no water or waves, only a bright and clear bridge. He stepped onto the bridge and looked ahead, seeing what seemed to be a human dwelling.

[P6] 8 The stone monkey crossed the bridge and, upon approaching, saw a stone cave. Inside were stone stoves, stone bowls, stone basins, stone beds, and stone stools. In the center stood a stone tablet inscribed with the words: 'The Blessed Land of Flower-Fruit Mountain, the Heavenly Cave of the Water Curtain.'
9 The stone monkey was overjoyed and hurriedly pulled himself out, leaping from the water. The other monkeys gathered around and asked, 'What's inside? How deep is the water?' The stone monkey laughed, 'What good fortune! What good fortune! Inside there is no water, and it's a wonderful place to live!' He then told them everything in detail.

[P7] 10 The monkeys all wanted to move in, saying, 'You go first, lead us in!' The Stone Monkey leaped in and said, 'Follow me!' The big and small monkeys one by one followed him in.
11 Upon reaching the stone cave, the monkeys scrambled for bowls and pots, fought over stoves and beds, moving things around until they were exhausted.

[P8] 12 The Stone Monkey sat on top and said, 'You all said whoever has the ability to enter shall be made king. I have now come and gone freely, and found this wonderful dwelling for you. Shouldn't I be made king?' Upon hearing this, the monkeys immediately bowed upward and called him 'His Majesty, the Thousand-Year King'.
13 From then on, the Stone Monkey was called the 'Beautiful Monkey King'. He assigned roles of lords, ministers, and attendants. He roamed the Flower-Fruit Mountain by day and rested in the Water-Curtain Cave by night, living a most joyful life. One day, while feasting with the monkeys, he suddenly shed tears.

[P9] 14 The monkeys hurriedly bowed and asked the reason. It turned out the Monkey King felt that although they were not subject to human laws and feared no beasts, once they grew old and died, they would still be controlled by King Yan. Upon hearing this, all the monkeys felt sorrowful.
15 Suddenly, a long-backed ape jumped out and shouted: 'Your Majesty, do not weep. I have heard that Buddhas, immortals, gods, and sages can escape the cycle of rebirth, are neither born nor die, and live as long as heaven and earth. Why not seek the art of immortality?' The Monkey King was overjoyed upon hearing this. He decided to go down the mountain tomorrow to search everywhere.

[P10] 16 The next morning, after the Monkey King had finished his farewell feast, he asked the other monkeys to weave a raft from dry branches, took a bamboo pole as a paddle, loaded it with some fruits and food, climbed aboard alone, pushed off with the paddle, and drifted gently out to sea.
17 For several days, the southeast wind blew, and in no time it carried him to the northwest shore. This was the territory of the Southern Continent. When he stepped ashore, he saw people by the sea fishing, hunting geese, and making salt... He walked up to them, made a funny face, and scared them all away.

[P11] 18 Among them, one who ran slowly was caught. The Monkey King stripped off his clothes, put them on himself, and swaggered about, imitating human manner, traveling from state to state, seeking the way of immortality.
19 In the blink of an eye, eight or nine years had passed. One day, while traveling, he arrived at the territory of the Western Ox贺洲. He heard singing from deep within the forest: '...Wherever we meet, it's either an immortal or a sage, sitting quietly and reciting the Huangting.' He thought: 'Huangting' is a true moral teaching; this person must be a god.

[P12] 20 He walked over and saw that it was a woodcutter chopping firewood. After the Monkey King explained his purpose, the woodcutter said: 'I am not a immortal, but I live next to immortals. This song was taught to me by them. If you have troubles or sorrows, singing it will naturally relieve your worries.'
21 The Monkey King was overjoyed and asked the woodcutter to point out where the immortals lived. The woodcutter pointed ahead and said: 'In the mountains ahead, there is a cave called Xieyue Sansxing Cave. Inside lives an immortal named Master Subodhi. He has taught countless disciples, and now still has thirty or forty people practicing with him.'

[P13] 22 The Monkey King walked in the direction the woodcutter pointed, about seven or eight li away, and indeed found a cave. The cave door was tightly shut, and it was quiet and empty. Looking up, he saw ten large characters on a stone tablet at the cliff's edge: 'Lingtai Fangcun Mountain, Xieyue Sanxing Cave'.
23 The Monkey King stared for a while, too afraid to knock. At that moment, he felt a bit hungry, so he jumped onto a pine tree and picked some pine nuts to eat. Just as he was eating, he heard a 'ya' sound, and from the opening cave door, a fairy child stepped out.

[P14] 24 The fairy child shouted: 'Who is disturbing here?' The Monkey King hurriedly jumped down and said: 'I am a disciple seeking immortality and Dao. I dare not disturb here.' The fairy child said: 'My master said a cultivator has come from outside, so I was sent to receive you. It's you! Come with me quickly.'
25 The Monkey King entered the cave and saw Master Puti sitting on a platform teaching, with thirty small fairies standing below on both sides. Upon seeing him, the Monkey King bowed deeply,磕头 countless times, and kept saying: 'Master! Master! Your humble disciple pays heartfelt respects, heartfelt respects.'

[P15] 26 The Master asked, 'Where are you from? What is your surname and name?' The Monkey King replied, 'I come from the Eastern Continent. I was born from a stone and have no name.' The Master said, 'Since you have traveled far to come here, I will take you as my disciple!' and gave him the name 'Sun Wukong'.
27 With a name now, the Beautiful Monkey King was extremely delighted. Every day he studied speech and manners with his fellow disciples, discussed scriptures and the Dao; in his spare time he swept the floor, tilled the garden, cultivated flowers, and pruned trees, and before he knew it, six or seven years had passed in the cave.

[P16] 28 One day, the Master ascended the platform to lecture, and all the immortals listened attentively. Sun Wukong, however, grew more and more delighted as he listened, scratching his ears and cheeks, beaming with joy, and could not help but dance.
29 The Master was deeply engrossed in his lecture when he suddenly saw Wukong in this state, and he shouted: 
"You are not listening attentively, why are you acting so wildly and dancing?" Wukong hurriedly replied: "Disciple truly listens with sincerity, only because I heard something wonderful, I could not contain my joy. I beg for Master's forgiveness!"

[P17] 30 The Master said, 'If so, then tell me what kind of Dao you wish to learn?' Wukong replied, 'Whatever my Master teaches me.' The Master then explained to him the several schools of Dao: 'Technique,' 'School,' 'Stillness,' and 'Movement.' Wukong felt these schools could not grant immortality and refused to study them.
31 The Master gave a loud 'Dong!' and jumped down from the lecture platform, holding his disciplinary ruler, pointing at Wukong and saying, 'You won't study this, nor that—what exactly do you want to learn?' He stepped forward, struck Wukong three times on the head, turned his back, walked inside, closed the middle gate, and left the crowd behind.

[P18] 32 The elder disciples saw their master in this state and blamed Wukong. Wukong was not at all upset, for he had already solved the riddle: he knew that hitting him three times meant meeting at the third watch; turning his back and closing the middle door meant he should enter through the back door to receive secret teachings.
33 That night, after Wukong and the other disciples had fallen asleep, he quietly got up, put on his clothes, opened the front door secretly, and went out.

[P19] 34 Wukong walked to the back door, saw it slightly ajar, pushed it open, and went in. He reached the master's bed and saw the master already sleeping with his back to him. Wukong dared not disturb him, so he knelt before the bed and waited.
35 After a while, the master woke up. Wukong hurried forward and said, 'Master, your disciple has been waiting here for a long time.' The master shouted, 'Why aren't you sleeping in the front, but coming here to the back?' Wukong replied, 'Master, yesterday before the altar you allowed me to come here at the third watch through the back door to receive your teachings, so I dared to come.'

[P20] 36 The Master was overjoyed upon hearing this, thinking to himself: 'This monkey is truly born of heaven and earth! Otherwise, how could he have solved the riddle in my palm?' He then said to Wukong, 'It is fate that we meet. I shall now pass on the secret of immortality to you!' And so, he taught Wukong the immortal mantra.
37 After learning the secret of immortality, Wukong bowed to thank his Master, then quietly slipped back through the rear door to the front. By then, dawn had broken. He sat in his original sleeping spot and deliberately shouted loudly, 'It's morning! It's morning! Get up!' All his fellow disciples were awakened by his shout.

[P21] 38 Wukong studied Dao in the mountains, and before he knew it, three more years had passed. One day, the Master ascended the platform and asked Wukong, "How is your study going?" Wukong stepped forward and bowed, saying, "Disciple's Dao nature is now quite proficient, and the root is gradually becoming stable." The Master replied, "Very good, but you must guard against the 'Three Calamities'.
39 Wukong thought deeply and said, "I have already cultivated immortality; what do I fear from the Three Calamities?" The Master replied, "This is an extraordinary path. Five hundred years from now, heavenly thunder will strike you; another five hundred years, heavenly fire will burn you; and another five hundred years, heavenly wind will blow you away! You must find a way to avoid them."

[P22] 40 Wukong, upon hearing this, was frightened and hurriedly knelt, saying: 'I beg Master to teach me the method to avoid the Three Calamities; I will never forget your kindness!' Seeing Wukong's sincerity, the Patriarch said: 'Very well, come closer and listen.' Then he taught him the incantation for the Seventy-Two Transformations.
41 After obtaining the Dao, Wukong studied and practiced diligently every day, gradually becoming proficient. One day, the Patriarch and his disciples were enjoying the evening view before the Sanxing Cave, and he asked Wukong: 'How is your practice coming along?"

[P23] 42 Wukong said, 'Disciple has mastered the skill and can now ascend on clouds.' The Master replied, 'Very good. Show me your flight.' Wukong leaped into the air, did a series of somersaults, rose five or six zhang above the ground, and soared away on the clouds.
43 After about the time of a meal, he returned, having traveled no more than three li round-trip, landing right before them. The Master laughed, 'This is not true cloud-sailing; it's merely crawling on clouds. True cloud-sailing, from dawn till dusk, can traverse all four seas. Your skill is still far from sufficient!'

[P24] 44 Wukong knelt and bowed three times, saying, 'Master, I beg you to show great mercy and teach me the art of flying at once!' The Master replied, 'All immortals take flight by stamping their feet, but you are not like that. Given your posture, I shall teach you the “Cloud Somersault” instead!'
45 After whispering the incantation for the “Cloud Somersault” into Wukong’s ear, the Master said, 'Just recite the true words, clench your fists, shake your body, jump up, and with one somersault, you can travel a hundred and eight thousand li!' Upon hearing this, everyone envied Wukong’s remarkable talent.

[P25] 46 One day, several disciples gathered under a pine tree to discuss their studies. After finishing, they turned to Wukong and said, 'Wukong, you're so lucky! Our master taught you the method to avoid the Three Calamities and transform. How well have you practiced it? Show us what you can do!' 
47 Wukong replied, 'I won't hide it from you, brothers. I've practiced day and night, and now I've mastered it all. You give me a challenge, and I'll show you what I can do.' Everyone said, 'Turn into a pine tree!' Wukong chanted the incantation, and with a twist of his body, he truly transformed into a pine tree.

[P26] 48 Everyone saw Wukong turn into a pine tree and clapped their hands in approval. Unintentionally, they startled the Master, who came out and asked, 'Who is making such a racket here?' Seeing the Master, everyone straightened their clothes and stepped forward. Wukong also revealed his true form and hid behind others, saying, 'Respected Master, we are merely gathering here to discuss, and there is no outsider causing disturbance.'
49 The Master angrily said, 'You don't look like people practicing cultivation at all!' Seeing the Master angry, everyone told him about Wukong turning into a pine tree. The Master then said, 'Since that's the case, you all go first. Wukong, stay here—I have something to say to you.'

[P27] 50 The Master called Wukong forward and said, 'Why did you turn into a pine tree? Showing off your skills in front of others is nothing but arrogance and self-satisfaction!' Wukong hurriedly knelt and admitted his mistake.
51 The Master said, 'I won't blame you. Go back to the Water Curtain Cave quickly. Remember, your skills are only to be used for justice and righteousness, never for wrongdoing.' Wukong replied, 'Master, how could I forget your words? I only feel uneasy because I haven't repaid your kindness yet!' The Master said, 'As long as you keep me in your heart, that's enough. Go now!'

[P28] 52 Wukong, helpless, could only thank his master, recite the incantation, and leap onto the 'Cloud of Somersault', returning to Flower-Fruit Mountain.
53 In less than an hour, he saw the Water Curtain Cave on Flower-Fruit Mountain, so he pressed down his cloud, landed on the mountain, and shouted loudly: 'Children, I'm back!'

[P29] 54 At this moment, monkeys of all sizes jumped out from under the cliffs, among the flowers and trees, and from the forest, surrounding Wukong and asking him all sorts of questions. They were so happy!
55 Some of the monkeys then told Wukong about their troubles, saying that a tyrant named Hunshi Wang often came to bully them, steal their belongings, kidnap their young, and even tried to seize the Water Curtain Cave! Upon hearing this, Wukong angrily said, “Where does he live? I’ll go and take revenge!”

[P30] 56 The monkeys pointed out the direction from which the Demon King of Chaos had come to Wukong. He then vanished with a single 'Cloud Somersault'.
57 Wukong was walking on the clouds. From above, he saw several small demons dancing below the cliff. He thought: This must be the place.

[P31] 58 Wukong landed, scaring the little demons into running away. Wukong said, “Don’t run! Go quickly and tell your Demon King of Chaos that the Master of the Water Curtain Cave from Flower-Fruit Mountain has come to settle accounts with him.”
59 The little demons rushed into the cave to report to the Demon King. The Demon King said, “Bring me my armor and weapons quickly!” The Demon King put on his armor, took a large sword, and came out of the cave with his followers. He shouted, “Which Master of the Water Curtain Cave is this? Dare to cause trouble here?”

[P32] 60 Wukong said: 'You evil demon, you can't recognize me, please take a few punches from me!' 
Saying that, he swung his fist. The Demon King raised his big knife and slashed at Wukong.
61 Wukong saw the fierce attack and couldn't withstand it, so he used the 'body-outside-body' technique, plucked a handful of hairs, chewed them in his mouth, spat them out, shouted 'Change!', and instantly turned them into two or three hundred monkeys who surrounded the Demon King.

[P33] 62 These monkeys pulled and hugged, immediately knocking the demon king down. Wukong came over, seized the big knife, separated the little monkeys, and struck the demon king on the top of his head, splitting him in two. Then, they killed all the demons in the cave.
63 He then shook his hair, and all the monkeys were gathered back onto his body. Those who were not gathered were the ones the demon king had captured from the Water Curtain Cave. After the monkeys explained the situation, Wukong said, "Since you are all descendants of the Water Curtain Cave, let's go back together!" The monkeys were overjoyed.

[P34] 64 Before leaving, Wukong set fire to the demon cave, then called dozens of little monkeys, closed their eyes, chanted a spell, rode a fierce wind, and headed straight for the Water Curtain Cave.
65 Upon reaching the cave entrance, Wukong said: 'Children, open your eyes.' The monkeys recognized their homeland, were delighted, and all rushed back into the cave.

[P35] 66 The monkeys reunite with their families, and the Monkey King returns from his journey, bringing double joy. They bring out various fine wines and fresh fruits, and everyone happily drinks together in celebration. Afterwards, Wukong trains his monkey soldiers to protect Flower-Fruit Mountain. For more details, please see the second volume, 'Borrowing the Treasure from the Dragon Palace'.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《猴王出世》的封面，展示了孙悟空的形象，并标明了作品名称、原著作者、改编者、绘画者及出版社信息。
[P2] 本页为绘本《猴王出世》的第2页，上半部分是内容提要，介绍了该连环画的创作背景及第一册的主要情节，即孙悟空的诞生、学艺与称王；下半部分是第一幅图画及其文字说明，描绘了古代东胜神州傲来国海边的花果山。
[P3] 本页描绘了花果山顶的仙石吸收天地精华化作石猴的过程，以及石猴在山中自由自在、与野兽为伴的生活情景。
[P4] 本页描绘了石猴与群猴在炎热天气下到山涧洗澡，随后决定顺流而上寻找水源源头，并在瀑布前提出‘谁敢钻进瀑布找到源头并安然无恙归来，就拜他为王’的挑战。
[P5] 石猴勇敢地跳入瀑布，发现瀑布后是一处无水的洞天，并看到一座桥和疑似有人居住的地方。
[P6] 石猴发现瀑布后隐藏的石洞，洞内有石制家具和刻有“花果山福地，水帘洞洞天”的石碑。他兴奋地跳出洞外，向众猴描述洞内景象，称其为理想的居所。
[P7] 石猴带领群猴进入水帘洞，众猴在洞内争抢家具、床铺，直到疲倦才停止。
[P8] 石猴成功找到水帘洞后，被众猴拜为‘千岁大王’，从此被称为‘美猴王’。他分派了君臣职位，与群猴在洞中饮宴，生活快活，但突然落泪。
[P9] 美猴王因担忧死亡而落泪，众猴悲伤。通背猿猴建议他寻求长生不老之术，猴王大喜，决定下山寻访。
[P10] 美猴王独自乘筏出海，乘东南风抵达南赡部洲海岸，上岸后吓跑正在捕鱼、打雁、淘盐的当地人。
[P11] 美猴王在南赡部洲偷得人衣，学人模样四处寻访仙道，八九年后抵达西牛贺洲，听到有人诵读《黄庭经》，认定其为神仙。
[P12] 美猴王在西牛贺洲遇到一位樵夫，向其打听神仙住处。樵夫告知他前方山中有斜月三星洞，住着神仙须菩提祖师，并指引方向。
[P13] 美猴王按樵夫指引找到斜月三星洞，洞门紧闭，他不敢敲门，便摘松子充饥，此时洞门开启，走出一个仙童。
[P14] 美猴王在斜月三星洞外被仙童发现，自称访仙学道弟子，仙童带他入洞。洞内菩提祖师正在讲道，猴王见后跪拜磕头，虔诚求师。
[P15] 美猴王拜菩提祖师为师，被赐名孙悟空，并在洞中与师兄们学习礼仪、讲经论道，闲时劳作，不知不觉过了六七年。
[P16] 孙悟空在菩提祖师讲道时因听得入迷而忍不住舞蹈，被祖师发现后，他解释是因听到妙处而喜不自胜，请求原谅。
[P17] 孙悟空向菩提祖师求学，祖师传授‘术’、‘流’、‘静’、‘动’等道门，但悟空因认为不能长生不老而拒绝学习。祖师生气，用戒尺敲了他三下后离开，将门关上。
[P18] 孙悟空破解了菩提祖师敲打三下、倒背手关门的暗语，明白师父是在三更时分于后门传授秘道，于是当晚趁众师兄熟睡时，悄悄穿好衣服，从后门离开。
[P19] 孙悟空按菩提祖师暗语，在三更时分从后门进入祖师寝室内跪候。祖师醒来后责问其为何不在前边睡觉，孙悟空解释是遵照师父昨日允诺前来求道。
[P20] 菩提祖师因孙悟空破解暗语而大喜，传授其长生口诀；孙悟空学成后悄悄返回，天亮时故意大喊唤醒众师兄。
[P21] 孙悟空在山中学道三年后，菩提祖师询问其修行进展，孙悟空表示法性已通，祖师提醒他需防‘三灾利害’。孙悟空不解，祖师解释三灾分别为雷、火、风，每五百年一次，需设法躲避。
[P22] 孙悟空请求菩提祖师传授躲避三灾之法，祖师见其诚心，便传授了七十二变的口诀。此后，悟空勤学苦练，技艺渐精，祖师在三星洞前询问其修炼进展。
[P23] 孙悟空向菩提祖师展示学成的飞行本领，但祖师认为其仅能‘爬云’，远未达到‘腾云’的境界，指出其技艺尚浅。
[P24] 孙悟空恳求菩提祖师传授腾云之法，祖师根据其姿态传授了“筋斗云”，并告知其口诀和威力，众弟子听后无不羡慕。
[P25] 孙悟空的师兄弟们在松树下聚会后，向他挑战展示所学的七十二变，孙悟空应允并当场变身为一棵松树，成功展示了他的变化之术。
[P26] 孙悟空在师兄弟们面前展示七十二变，变身为松树，引起众人喝彩，却惊动了菩提祖师。祖师责问后，让其他弟子离开，单独留下孙悟空谈话。
[P27] 菩提祖师责备孙悟空在师兄弟面前炫耀七十二变，将其叫到跟前训诫，并允许他返回水帘洞，叮嘱他所学本领只能行侠仗义，不可胡作非为。孙悟空表示铭记师恩，祖师最终放他离去。
[P28] 孙悟空在菩提祖师的训诫后，无奈告别师父，驾筋斗云返回花果山，并在抵达后向众猴宣告归来。
[P29] 孙悟空返回花果山后，众猴围住他问好，其中一些猴子向他诉说混世魔王欺压猴群、强占水帘洞的苦楚，孙悟空听后怒不可遏，决心前去报仇。
[P30] 孙悟空在众猴指引下，驾筋斗云前往混世魔王的巢穴，途中发现山崖下有小妖跳舞，确认了目的地。
[P31] 孙悟空降落到混世魔王的巢穴附近，吓跑小妖并命令其通报；混世魔王得知后披挂兵器，率众出洞，高声质问来者是谁。
[P32] 孙悟空与混世魔王交战，先出拳攻击，后见对方攻势猛烈，便施展身外身法术，变出二三百只猴子围住魔王。
[P33] 孙悟空在众猴协助下击败混世魔王，将其斩杀，并消灭洞中所有妖魔。随后他收起变出的猴子，将被掳走的猴群带回水帘洞，众猴欣喜若狂。
[P34] 孙悟空烧毁混世魔王的洞穴后，带着众猴驾风返回水帘洞，抵达后唤醒众猴，猴子们认出家乡，欣喜地奔入洞中。
[P35] 孙悟空击败混世魔王后，与猴群在花果山团圆，大家欢庆饮酒。页面下方附有《西游记》连环画的完整目录。
